question: Pentagon or SpaceX: who made the call?
hook_lines: MUSK: US MILITARY SET STARLINK LIMITS

lines.text: Elon Musk says the US military, not SpaceX, decides the Starlink limits that hit Ukraine's troops.
The system is Starshield, the military version of Starlink, built by SpaceX.
Overnight on Tuesday, Ukraine says terminals moving faster than 160 kilometres an hour lost their link.
Some units say the link dropped at speeds as low as 72.
Near Huliaipole, drones lost contact for up to twenty seconds, and some missions were suspended.
Musk wrote: Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government.

scene.quote: Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government

lines.text: Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military, and ultimately the president.

scene.quote: Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS

lines.text: But a senior White House official told Axios the administration had no role in it.
Republican senator Thom Tillis wants the Pentagon's inspector general to investigate.
He says the snafu may have happened more locally within Pentagon Starshield systems.
lines.note: Tillis on X, via The Hill

scene.quote: may have occurred more locally within DOD Starshield systems, not with Starlink or SpaceX

lines.text: Zelensky called the loss a big mistake.
By Thursday morning, Ukraine's defence ministry says Starshield on the move is working again.
What caused the cut, and whether any limit remains, is still not clear.
Pentagon or SpaceX: who made the call?
